result.informal_name: Decidability of Diagonal Membership in Symmetric Squares
result.informal_description: For any type $\alpha$ with decidable equality, the predicate that determines whether an element of the symmetric square $\mathrm{Sym}^2(\alpha)$ belongs to the diagonal subset (i.e., is represented by a pair $(a,a)$) is decidable. This follows because an element $[a,b] \in \mathrm{Sym}^2(\alpha)$ lies in the diagonal subset if and only if $a = b$, and equality in $\alpha$ is decidable.
